one_sentence: This document argues that ten fundamental physical laws have isomorphic spiritual counterparts, with the single added term of free will distinguishing the spiritual domain from the physical.
executive_summary: This document presents the Ten Laws framework, which claims that each of ten fundamental physical laws (gravity, mass-energy, electromagnetism, strong force, thermodynamics, information, relativity, quantum mechanics, weak force, and coherence) has a direct spiritual analog (grace, meaning, truth, love, moral entropy, Logos, relationship, faith, sin-decay, and Christ). The core structural claim is that the spiritual versions are identical to the physical equations except for a single added free-will term that makes the spiritual domain an offer rather than a compulsion. The key evidence is the mathematical isomorphism between the equations, the consistent placement of the asymmetry term, and computational verification including Hessian matrix rankings. The conclusion is that the universe of souls is not compulsory like the universe of rocks, and that the integrated maximum of all nine laws converges to identity with Christ (Law 10). This matters because it provides a falsifiable, mathematically grounded framework for relating physics and theology.
short_summary: This document is a canonical treatment of the Ten Laws framework, presenting ten physical laws and their spiritual counterparts. The core structural claim is that each spiritual law is isomorphic to its physical counterpart except for a single free-will term that converts compulsion into offer. Key evidence includes the mathematical equations, the asymmetry table, and computational results such as Hessian rankings. This matters because it offers a testable, rigorous isomorphism between physics and theology that can be verified or falsified.
